source_scope: 16 selected production, ABI, adapter, test and build inputs match the Linux workspace byte-for-byte; not a hermetic whole-worktree release manifest.

execution.runtime: root native host CLI, private MTU-1500 veth pair, two worker network namespaces sharing one selected cgroup

findings.change: Add reproducible cross-namespace and real kernel-fragmented UDP acceptance. No product runtime fix needed in these bounded runs.
development_attempts: attempt-1: ip netns exec remounted sysfs and hid the selected cgroup; fixture fixed to native setns with thread-local proc counters
attempt-2: passed before adding exact interface-index checking; not counted among final runs
findings.namespace_identity: Both peers reuse veth ifindex 2 but have distinct run-local namespace IDs. IDs are not stable across captures.
findings.fragmentation: Kernel fragment/reassembly counters establish actual MTU pressure. Product hook observations are normalized datagrams, not raw fragment capture or product-owned reassembly.

summary_projection: Expected packet prefix arrays are omitted here to avoid duplicating raw exports; original worker oracles, observed reports and full summaries remain under evidence_root. SHA-256 below binds original summary bytes, not this projection.

validation.clippy_command: cargo --config profile.dev.package.gewyvern.opt-level=2 clippy --locked --test production_capture_linux_tdd --test native_validation_harness_tdd -- -D warnings
validation.status_validation_scope: Catalog consistency and declared GUI target coverage, not overall product readiness.

limits: Single host and private veth, not physical-link, multiple-host or sustained-load certification.
Payloads above 128 bytes retain only their prefix. Native peer full-I/O hashes are not product full-payload hashes.
No raw-fragment archival or product-owned reassembly; no malformed, overlapping, missing-fragment, arbitrary IPv6 extension, checksum, NAT or GSO/GRO claim.
Namespace IDs are run-local. Full IP endpoints, kernel namespace-cookie mappings and authenticated process lineage are not retained.
No release-artifact, protocol-count or status-maturity promotion.
